title: Predictive Commitment Mixer and Fallthrough Throttle
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: we continue to see oscillation and overcommit during multi-tenant decommit windows and low-SLA bursts. Current autoscaler reacts to raw utilization signals which amplifies transients and leads to unnecessary instance churn or emergency fallback to higher-cost pools. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms: 1) Predictive Commitment Mixer (PCM) — a runtime component that synthesizes short-term demand forecasts with observed utilization and the tenant's commitment profile to compute conservative commit/decommit recommendations; 2) Fallthrough Throttle — a probabilistic, rate-limited fallback path that gradually routes overflow to lower-cost models/pools while preserving tail throughput SLOs.

High level changes: - PCM blends three signals (EWMA demand forecast, active request percentiles, and commitment slack) using tunable weights and a capped smoothing window. The result is a per-tenant target commit delta that reduces oscillation and enforces a minimum grace budget during decommit waves. - Fallthrough Throttle implements a per-tenant token-bucket that gates how quickly requests are redirected to fallthrough pools. Tokens are replenished based on sampled utilization percentiles to prioritize throughput SLO preservation. A probabilistic selection function avoids synchronized redirects across tenants. - Utilization Sampling Proxy: to limit high-cardinality metrics, this component takes reservoir-sampled snapshots of active-concurrency and p95/p99 service times and emits compact rollups to the fleet telemetry pipeline. This preserves tail signals used by PCM while reducing cardinality and egress cost by ~60% in our internal canary. - Feature-flagged rollout and canary hooks: all behavior lives behind runtime flags and a canary configuration that pins a small subset of Dedicated pools and tenants.

Why this is different: unlike simple hysteresis/autoscale hysteresis, PCM explicitly fuses forecasted demand with contractual commitment and introduces a controlled decommit cadence. The Fallthrough Throttle focuses on graceful capacity shedding rather than immediate spillover, which reduces cascading latency spikes. The Sampling Proxy is designed to preserve percentile fidelity required for SLO guarantees while reducing telemetry volume.

b3f4a18: implement EWMA demand forecast and percentile collector

review_comments: Diego Morales: Overall strong design. Please add integration tests that simulate correlated tenant decommits across AZs and verify no more than 10% extra capacity is provisioned during the window.
Ava Chen (author): Added e2e harness simulating correlated decommits; see test/e2e/predictive_mixer_stability_test.go. Test parameterized for 100/500/1000 tenant mixes.
Priya Nair: Backoff formula looks aggressive for low-latency tenants (p95 < 50ms). Recommend adding a min_commit floor per SLA tier.
Ava Chen: Added per-tenant min_commit floor derived from SLA tier mapping and respected by the mixer. Defaults to conservative values; exposed as runtime knobs.
Liam O'Connor: Telemetry cardinality concern seems addressed by sampling proxy; please include a short benchmark of emitted series per-minute across 10k tenants.
Ava Chen: Added benchmark notes in docs and a small benchmark script in internal/canary that showed ~62% reduction in emitted series at 10k tenants under our sample config.
Priya Nair: Suggest making the probabilistic selector seed deterministic per-tenant to aid reproducible canary debugging.
Ava Chen: Updated selector to include tenant id salt + feature-flagged deterministic mode.

End-to-end canary deployment built and smoke-tested in staging. Lint and vet checks passed. Observability job validated emitted rollups. Full CI run: 1/1 failed -> rerun -> pass; final status: pass.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash-merge on 2026-02-25. Commit message consolidated: "Predictive Commitment Mixer + Fallthrough Throttle: reduced autoscale oscillation, added sampling proxy, feature-flagged rollout." Release: behind feature flag; opt-in canary enabled for 5% of Dedicated pools.
release_notes: Introduces Predictive Commitment Mixer and Fallthrough Throttle (feature-flagged). Reduces autoscaler oscillation during decommit windows and adds a telemetry sampling proxy for lower metrics cardinality. Default behavior is disabled; to opt-in see docs/dedicated/autoscale-predictive-mixer.md.
